title: Indexing embeddings: approximate indexes and HNSW

videos.script: Exact search reads every vector for every question. {{linear}} At a hundred thousand vectors, that is a hundred thousand comparisons, each one a long sum. Double the collection and you double the wait. This lesson is about the indexes that refuse to read everything. {{skip}} To skip a vector, an index has to guess that it cannot be among the nearest. Sometimes the guess is wrong. So you will start with recall: how many of the true neighbours an index still finds. {{recall}} Then the first trick. Sort the vectors into cells, and search only the cells near the question. {{cells}} Then the one most databases use, HNSW. A graph of neighbours, in layers, that a search walks down from the top. {{layers}} You will trace one search by hand, layer by layer, and count its comparisons. A few hundred, out of a hundred thousand. {{trace}} Every one of these indexes has a dial. Turn it up and recall rises, and so does the time. {{curve}} You will measure both sides, and see why the last few neighbours are the expensive ones. And you will shrink the vectors inside the index, and find where that is free and where it is not. {{codes}}
